text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- First preliminary results on voting for municipal and county assemblies across Croatia show the ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) in a commanding lead in all counties except Istria.
- In the elections for the Zagreb City Assembly HDZ has a relative majority over the opposition coalition.
- The U.N. extended the elections in the Serb-run enclave of Eastern Slavonia till Monday evening due to initial technical delays.
- Voters' turnout is put at more than 70 percent, according to unofficial results.

- On-line trading system of the Zagreb Stock Exchange, launched last Tuesday, immediately brought a new daily record of 214 transactions. Over-the-counter market in Varazdin also to introduce on-line trading in May.
- Some 22 percent of the interviewed beneficiaries of the mass privatisation say they will entrust their vouchers to investment funds for management.
- Insurer Adriatic Osiguranje, a subsidiary of Zagrebacka Banka, plans to expand the range of services this year.

- Police and customs in the Adriatic port of Rijeka on Sunday confiscated 38 kg (85 lb) of cocaine a day after discovering 150 kg (330 lb) of the drug in the port. Value of the two seizures put at $10 million. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
